agent_audits.name: once_cell
agent_audits.notes:
Проверено агентом, не человеком. AI full production source review by Codex; not an independent human audit.
Published archive SHA-256: 9f7c3e4beb33f85d45ae3e3a1792185706c8e16d043238c593331cc7cd313b50.
Read both manifests, complete archive inventory and all five production Rust modules, including their unsafe contracts, feature selection, generated documentation examples and imp_std unit tests. No build script, native code, network, filesystem, environment reads or subprocess authority in the library. Initializer closures are caller-supplied Rust functions, not evaluated text.
For unsync cells, UnsafeCell<Option<T>> is written only after checking emptiness, without invoking user code while a mutable slot reference exists; get_or_try_init computes the callback first and then asserts that reentrant initialization did not already fill the cell. Mutation/take/into_inner require exclusive access or ownership. Lazy consumes its FnOnce exactly once and consistently panics after poisoning.
For sync cells, checked get acquires publication before get_unchecked. Send/Sync bounds include both T: Send and T: Sync where shared cells can transfer destruction between threads. Lazy only needs F: Send because F is consumed by the serialized initializer and is never shared as &F. The std backend uses the low two bits of a 4-byte-aligned waiter pointer for state, an atomic CAS for a single initializer, and release/acquire publication of the value and linked stack waiters. Guard drop resets state on error/panic, detaches the waiter list, reads each next/thread before the release signal allows that waiter to return, and unparks its cloned thread handle. Address tagging uses wrapping pointer offsets to retain provenance; marker pointers are never dereferenced. Waiting may block and recursive sync initialization may deadlock as documented; initializers must not depend on their own completion.
The parking_lot backend serializes initialization with INCOMPLETE/RUNNING/COMPLETE states; its guard publishes with Release and unparks on success or unwinding, with a validated park predicate to avoid missed wakeups. The critical-section backend delegates exclusion to critical_section, reuses the checked unsync initialization and Release/Acquire publication, and reads without a critical section only after immutable initialization is acquired. Correct implementations of critical_section, portable-atomic and parking_lot_core are separate dependency obligations.
Race cells use nonzero/null sentinels with Release CAS and Acquire loads/failure ordering. A losing OnceBox candidate is reconstructed and dropped once; the winner is reconstructed only under exclusive drop. OnceRef retains the source lifetime using invariant PhantomData<UnsafeCell<&T>> and requires T: Sync to be shared. OnceNonZeroUsize::get_unchecked permits a non-atomic read only under its explicit initialized-and-acquired precondition: successful writes cannot occur after initialization, and failed compare_exchange does not write. Unsafe get_unchecked APIs and caller callbacks retain their documented preconditions. No serious exploit identified for reasonable production use under these contracts.
Direct pinned rustc/rustdoc validation: five std backend unit tests and 42 doctests passed, one doctest ignored upstream; std+alloc+race, no-default and alloc+race libraries compiled. Optional backend sources were reviewed but their external-dependency builds, Miri, sanitizers, cross-platform CI and the larger upstream integration/stress suite were not run. This is a new safe-to-deploy review, not an upgrade of a fuzz safe-to-run audit. ADR 0104 continuation.

publisher_mechanics.finding: cargo-vet 0.10.4 regenerates required entries per package name across all locked versions. If one version has no path, it does not retain newly fetched paths/publisher records for other versions of that name. An unsuccessful unlocked check computes a lower gap count but saves no imports. Final counts use the locked repository wrapper only.
